digest.question: How can a flock move as one when no bird leads?

hookResult.text: Each bird follows a few simple rules about the birds near it, and the flock's motion emerges from them.

anchors.need: The paper's statement that flock motion emerges from each bird's local behaviours.

causalChain.claim: Each bird perceives only the flockmates near it.

anchors.need: The paper's argument that a flock member perceives only nearby flockmates, and why that locality matters.

causalChain.claim: Each bird balances three behaviours: avoid collisions, match velocity, and stay near the flock's centre.

anchors.need: The paper's statement of its three behaviours, and its description of collision avoidance.

causalChain.claim: The flock's coordinated motion emerges from these local behaviours, with no leader.

levels.title: A flock with no leader
levels.goal: Slide Move together, and watch the whole flock turn as one.

anchors.need: The paper's description of velocity matching: a bird matching the velocity of the flockmates near it.

counterfactual.prompt: What if birds ignored their neighbours' headings?
counterfactual.expectedQualitativeEffect: Within 20 seconds the left flock turns one colour, while the right one stays a confetti of colours, each bird on its own heading.

beginner.text: Each bird turns to match the way its neighbours are flying. No bird leads.
beginner.analogy: Like people leaving a stadium: each matches the pace and direction of those beside them, and nobody is in charge.

intermediate.text: Each step, a bird steers toward the average heading of the birds it can see. Move together sets how hard it steers.

advanced.text: Aᵢ = w_a (ūᵢ − vᵢ): bird i accelerates toward ūᵢ, the mean velocity of the birds it sees, at rate w_a, which is Move together.

guide.idle: No bird leads. Each one steers only by the few it can see.
guide.raised: You raised Move together{to}, so birds turn harder toward their neighbours' heading.
guide.lowered: You lowered Move together{to}, so birds care less which way their neighbours fly.
guide.atMinimum: At 0, no bird matches its neighbours' heading at all.

counterfactual.prompt: What if every bird could see the whole flock?
counterfactual.expectedQualitativeEffect: Seeing everyone does not bring order sooner in this model: on this seed the right flock agrees a little later than the left one.

beginner.text: No bird sees the whole flock. Each one reacts only to the birds near it, so a turn has to pass from bird to bird.
beginner.analogy: Like news in a crowd: each person hears only their neighbours, so it travels person to person.

intermediate.text: Moving together and staying close count only the birds within this distance. At a small distance, patches form, each with its own heading.

advanced.text: Nᵢ = { j ≠ i : |δᵢⱼ| < R }: alignment and cohesion average only over the birds within R of bird i, measured the short way round the world. Separation uses its own, smaller radius.

levels.title: Three urges, and the first: keep your distance
levels.goal: Change each bird's personal space, and watch the spacing.

anchors.need: The paper's statement of its three behaviours, and its description of collision avoidance.

counterfactual.prompt: What if birds never kept their distance?
counterfactual.expectedQualitativeEffect: Without personal space the right flock bunches tighter: its birds end up much closer together than the left one's.

beginner.text: A bird follows three urges: keep your distance, match your neighbours, stay with the flock. Personal space is the first. It stops collisions and sets how far apart birds fly.
beginner.analogy: Like people on a busy pavement, each keeping a step's distance from those around them.

intermediate.text: A bird steers away from any neighbour closer than its separation radius, 1.55 world units here. Personal space sets how quickly it steers away.

advanced.text: Sᵢ = w_s (v* sᵢ / |sᵢ| − vᵢ), where sᵢ sums −δᵢⱼ / |δᵢⱼ|² over the neighbours closer than R_s: a bird turns away from crowding, hardest from the nearest, at rate w_s, which is Personal space.

anchors.need: The paper's statement of its three behaviours, and its description of collision avoidance.

guide.raised: You gave each bird more personal space{to}, so it swerves sooner from a bird that comes too close.
guide.lowered: You shrank each bird's personal space{to}, so birds let others crowd in.
guide.atMinimum: At 0, birds do nothing to keep apart.

counterfactual.prompt: What if birds had no urge to stay together?
counterfactual.expectedQualitativeEffect: On this seed both worlds stay one group: in this model, matching headings holds the flock together even without the pull toward the middle.

beginner.text: The third urge: steer toward the middle of the birds you can see. It pulls stragglers back toward the others.
beginner.analogy: Like friends in a crowd drifting back toward each other when they get separated.

intermediate.text: Each step, a bird steers toward the centre of the birds within its sight. Stay close sets how quickly. A group is birds linked within 4.5 world units and flying within 45° of each other, 4 birds or more.

advanced.text: Cᵢ = w_c (v* cᵢ / max(|cᵢ|, r_c) − vᵢ), where cᵢ is the mean offset to the birds bird i sees: it steers toward their centre at rate w_c, which is Stay close, easing off within r_c.

levels.title: Does it behave like a flock?
levels.goal: Change how early birds swerve, and watch the flock pass the rock.

anchors.need: The paper's discussion of avoiding environmental obstacles, and its observation that flocks split around obstacles and re-form.

counterfactual.prompt: What if the rock pushed as hard as the model allows?
counterfactual.expectedQualitativeEffect: The right flock bursts apart at the rock, and its headings scatter before they agree again.

beginner.text: One way to judge a flock model is to put a rock in its way and watch. Nothing in the rules mentions rocks except a push away from them.
beginner.analogy: Like a stream flowing round a stone and joining up again behind it.

intermediate.text: A bird is pushed away from the rock once it comes within this distance. Nothing else is added: how the flock parts and re-forms comes from the three urges.

advanced.text: Oᵢ = Σ w_o (R_o − |δᵢₒ|)(−δᵢₒ / |δᵢₒ|) over rocks closer than R_o: the push starts R_o from the rock and grows linearly toward it. The model's rocks push like a force field; they do not steer a bird away ahead of time.

anchors.need: The paper's discussion of avoiding environmental obstacles, and its observation that flocks split around obstacles and re-form.

guide.lowered: You made birds swerve late{to}, so they come close to the rock before they turn.

levels.title: Order from the bottom up
levels.goal: Find the strength of Move together at which order appears.

counterfactual.prompt: What if the flock were a quarter as dense?
counterfactual.expectedQualitativeEffect: The sparser flock takes far longer to agree: on this seed it is still disordered after 20 seconds.

beginner.text: Below some strength of following, the flock stays disordered. Above it, order appears, and the change comes over a fairly small range of the control. No bird plans it.
beginner.analogy: Like a crowd starting to clap in time: below some eagerness to follow it stays ragged, and above it a rhythm takes hold.

intermediate.text: Change Move together a little at a time and watch the compass's arrow. A steep rise in agreement over a small change of the control marks a change from disorder to order.

advanced.text: φ = |(1/N) Σ vᵢ / |vᵢ||, the directional agreement. A steep rise of φ over a small change of w_a marks a transition from disorder to order.

guide.atMinimum: At 0, no bird follows its neighbours at all.

levels.carryForward: Order can appear from local rules alone, once following is strong enough.

limitations: A two-dimensional teaching adaptation of the paper's model, not a reproduction of its system or its results.
The rules are summed with weights and capped, a teaching choice; the levels say where that matters.
Rocks push birds like a force field rather than steering them away ahead of time.
Every level opens on one seed, chosen by a rule (ADR-0003). One run shows what these rules can do, not what they usually do.
A draft: its anchors are placeholders until the source map exists, and no passage is quoted yet.
